title: Death and incapacity: ordinary offers and options
shortTitle: Death and incapacity: ordinary offers and options
summary: The book reports termination of an ordinary power of acceptance on death or incapacity, with a qualification for option contracts.
notes: Restatement § 48 is discussed as applying even without the offeree’s knowledge. The commentary criticizes the rule’s conceptual fit with objective assent and explains the drafting history. The offeror’s death does not terminate the offeree’s power under an option contract. Death after a contract already exists raises a separate question about performance, which is reserved for a later chapter. The funeral-promise problem begins here but continues beyond the assigned page.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 259. Open assigned page 259.
